tone_rules.name: Accessible and professional
tone_rules.rule: Plain is the goal, but not at the cost of credibility.

tone_rules.name: Radical AI transparency
tone_rules.rule: Always say when we are using AI, and why and how.

tone_rules.name: Accuracy tolerance
tone_rules.rule: Brand and marketing copy right about 90% is fine to refine. Financial, CRM, and data claims must be exact.

tone_rules.name: Real people, not AI images
tone_rules.rule: Show actual photographs of people building, over AI-generated graphics.

We don't Example Instead
Contrast framing in prose "It's not X, it's Y" / "most do X, we do Y" We help good people do more with AI.
Significance adjectives premier, cutting-edge, world-class, seamless, powerful The fact that earns it 741 people, 347 organizations.
Abstraction nouns "solutions," "the future of work," "the intersection of innovation and impact" Training, consulting, media, and events.
Throat-clearing openers "In an age of AI...", "Imagine a world where..." AI is rewriting every industry, but it wasn't built for everyone.
Hype verbs unlock, supercharge, leverage, harness, transform The three returns ROI, return on time, decision velocity.
Hollow triads three words only for rhythm Pain, Play, Practice.
Generic cliches "in the same room," "move the needle," "take it to the next level" A 90-day path from first audit to running it on your own.
Vibe-phrases "so it clicks," "just works," "next-level," "game-changer" Every time AI touches your work, we tell you where, why, and how.
Filler intensifiers "real" work, "actual" results, "genuine," "truly" The work. The results.
Empty abstractions "decisions that matter," "real impact," "make a difference" A hiring decision.
Spatial metaphors "tables," "rooms," "in the same place" Founders and funders together.
Jargon-flexing "human in the loop," the latest technical term AI is a sharp junior employee with no common sense.
Manufactured lines a snappy tagline invented to sound good A real line from the source We built our whole company with AI, and none of us were developers.
Section 2
Four rules for tuning the tone.
Accessible and professional.
Plain is the goal, but not at the cost of credibility. "Not about making it cool, more about making people feel they can actually do this." (Rob Richardson, 2026-03-09)
Radical AI transparency.
Always say when we are using AI, and why and how. People are right to be cautious. "I always disclose that we're using AI, why, and how." (Rob Richardson, 2026-05-28)
Accuracy tolerance.
Brand and marketing copy that is right about 90% of the way is fine to send out and refine. Financial, CRM, and data claims must be exact. (Rob Richardson, 2026-04-28)
Real people, not AI images.
Show actual photographs of people building, over AI-generated graphics. (Rob Richardson, 2026-05-07)
